topic: For an arbitrary finite randomized design with rational positive assignment probabilities, binary potential-outcome schedule, assignment-specific observed-coordinate sets, and a fixed linear effect estimator, characterize all design-estimable expected variance bounds as the Boolean Mobius space generated by observable subsets; characterize finite pointwise conservativeness, the observable-margin LP dual, the Pareto-admissible class, exact higher-degree separation, tensorization, implementation, and conservative studentized inference within the finite binary scope.

open_problems.open_problem: For an arbitrary finite randomized design with positive rational assignment probabilities and binary potential outcomes, characterize exactly which expected variance-bound functionals are design-estimable in the full Boolean Mobius space and characterize every pointwise-minimal conservative bound.

source_refs.claim: Characterizes estimability and admissibility within quadratic-form variance bounds; quadratic estimability is controlled by pairwise design compatibility.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Provides a matrix framework for bounding and estimating the variance of linear estimators under arbitrary designs, but the represented bounds are quadratic.
source_refs.author: Joel A. Middleton

source_refs.excerpt: Vbar_n is a completion supremum, not minimal over quadratic-form variance estimators

open_problems.why_unsolved: Harshaw--Middleton--Savje prove an if-and-only-if estimability result and a complete admissible class only after restricting the candidate bound to a quadratic form, so observability is pairwise and conservativeness is expressed through quadratic domination. The prior ego-cluster run independently records that a completion supremum is not known to be minimal even among quadratic estimators. On a binary schedule every functional has a unique multilinear expansion, and assignment-specific observation sets can reveal higher-order subsets; the missing step is to replace pairwise compatibility by the full observable-subset complex and prove that pointwise domination, not positive-semidefinite domination, governs the complete class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if observable-support theorem for Boolean Mobius coefficients, a finite-cube pointwise-domination theorem, and an observable-margin primal-dual LP whose supporting weights characterize all Pareto-admissible conservative bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from unavoidable variance nonidentification to design compatibility and then to optimization over admissible bounds; that arc makes the higher-order departure legible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Missing joint potential outcomes prevent unbiased variance estimation -> the design determines which surrogate bounds are estimable -> quadratic compatibility yields an optimized admissible class -> binary outcomes call for the complete all-degree observable-subset class

method_exemplars.technique: Encode the true design variance as a known coefficient object, zero incompatible interactions, and use strictly monotone supporting objectives to characterize undominated feasible bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the exact degree-two analogue of the desired observable-subset Mobius characterization and supporting-weight complete-class theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use binary potential-outcome identities and inclusion-exclusion to sharpen an unidentified randomization variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired all-degree representation similarly turns Boolean identities into estimable bound terms unavailable for unrestricted real schedules.

method_exemplars.technique: Implement design-compatible interactions by inverse observation-probability weighting and control mean-square error using assignment dependence and coefficient norms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each observable Mobius monomial has the same implementation logic, with higher-order joint-observation events replacing pairs.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact degree hierarchy of universally conservative observable variance bounds for finite binary experiments, including whether the supplied six-coordinate three-atom design has quartic optimum 107/72 and degree-at-most-three optimum 55/36.

source_refs.claim: Its admissibility and optimization theory is confined to quadratic-form bounds, leaving strict improvements by observable nonquadratic functions untreated.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: For binary outcomes in a 2-by-2 factorial experiment, inclusion-exclusion gives a sharper variance bound than the classical Neyman construction.
source_refs.author: Jiannan Lu

source_refs.claim: Obtains asymptotically sharp complete-randomization variance bounds from observed potential-outcome marginals, not from an arbitrary-design polynomial-degree hierarchy.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, Donald K. K. Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing sharpness arguments use either a special complete-randomization coupling problem or a special factorial binary identity, while the closest arbitrary-design theory optimizes only over quadratic forms. None decides whether cubic or quartic observable monomials strictly improve a universally conservative rule for a general assignment-specific observation pattern. Complement symmetry can annihilate odd-degree gains, so the claimed quartic threshold and 1/24 separation require a symmetry reduction and matching exact rational primal and dual certificates; floating-point optimization is not a resolution.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A degree-filtration and complement-symmetry theorem plus independently checkable rational primal-dual certificates for all 64 domination inequalities proving 107/72, 55/36, and their exact 1/24 difference.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents optimized quadratic bounds as a finite-sample admissibility problem and is the natural foil for a result showing that the quadratic class is globally incomplete on binary schedules.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Variance contains unobservable products -> compatible quadratic surrogates can be optimized -> quadratic admissibility need not imply global admissibility on a binary cube -> a smallest exact design witnesses the first higher-degree gain

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit binary identities and inclusion-exclusion to turn restrictions on potential-outcome tables into a sharp finite-population variance inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target certificate likewise depends on Boolean cancellation unavailable for unrestricted real outcomes.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize compatible slack objects under monotone objectives and certify restricted-class admissibility through convex duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The degree hierarchy asks the analogous optimum question over nested Boolean-polynomial spaces.

method_exemplars.technique: Implement each observable interaction by inverse joint-observation weighting and prove its design expectation exactly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The quartic optimizer requires an assignment-level unbiased implementation with subset inclusion probabilities replacing pair inclusion probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a provably lossless, computationally manageable observable-margin decomposition for the Paluck--Shepherd--Aronow school-network exposure design that preserves its assignment law and direct-effect estimand while returning exact rational higher-order certificates.

source_refs.claim: Uses the 24,183-student, 56-school network data as an empirical simulation setting for quadratic OPT-VB and does not reanalyze the original causal conclusions.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Separates design, exposure mapping, and estimand under interference and develops randomization-based estimation and inference with American-school network data.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Cyrus Samii

source_refs.excerpt: exact oracle and regret programs can require enumeration of exponentially many balanced sign-pairs
Add a non-pair score geometry at n at least 8 with an enumerated kappa(S), gamma(S), threshold

open_problems.why_unsolved: The school design combines school-level assignment, within-treated-school seed assignment, and network exposure, so naive enumeration of assignments, binary schedules, and observable subsets is infeasible. The closest paper solves a quadratic semidefinite program numerically for an empirical illustration, whereas the all-degree Boolean program is an exponentially larger observable-margin LP and a floating-point solution is not an exact certificate. Prior CausalSmith work independently documents exponential enumeration in exact finite design programs. The first method step that must change is to replace global enumeration by orbit-, separator-, or bag-local Mobius states and prove that local consistency glues to global domination without altering the assignment law or estimand.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem for a lossless orbit, separator, or bounded-treewidth decomposition, together with a reduced rational LP whose lifted primal solution, dual weights, and assignment-level identities certify the unreduced school-design optimum.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the school-network problem through the separate roles of assignment design, exposure mapping, and estimand, keeping the computational target tied to the real experiment.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: School interventions spill through friendship networks -> exposure mappings translate assignments into interpretable conditions -> inverse-probability contrasts target direct and spillover effects -> exact higher-order variance optimization must preserve the same two-stage law and estimand

method_exemplars.technique: Construct design incompatibilities from the exposure mapping, optimize a compatible slack object, and certify admissibility with a strictly monotone objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It uses the same school-network substrate and supplies the quadratic optimization object that the reduced higher-order LP must strictly generalize.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute exposure probabilities under the known design, form inverse-probability effect and variance estimators, and prove validity under local dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The lifted implementation certificate must be expressed at the assignment and exposure level used by the actual school design.

open_problems.open_problem: Give verifiable triangular-array conditions under which an assignment-level implementation of an observable higher-order Pareto-optimal variance bound yields correctly scaled conservative studentized inference for a fixed linear causal-effect estimator.

source_refs.claim: Provides mean-square consistency conditions for Horvitz--Thompson implementations of compatible quadratic bounds, but not higher-order observable Boolean bounds.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Supplies finite-population central limit theorems for randomization-based causal estimators under multiple treatments, factors, and clustered designs.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Establishes consistency and asymptotic normality for inverse-probability exposure-effect estimators under local dependence and uses conservative randomization variance estimators.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Cyrus Samii

open_problems.why_unsolved: A higher-order bound estimator contains inverse probabilities for jointly observing entire subsets, so its variance and dependency neighborhood can grow much faster than in pairwise theory. A CLT for the effect estimator alone is insufficient: the random denominator must obey the correct normalization, remain nondegenerate, and converge to a quantity that asymptotically dominates the true design variance. Existing results separately cover numerator CLTs and consistency of particular quadratic or network variance estimators, but not their composition for all-degree observable-subset implementations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A design-based triangular-array theorem proving a CLT for the linear estimator, ratio or one-sided consistency of the scaled higher-order bound estimator, and conservative asymptotic Wald coverage under explicit boundedness, nondegeneracy, subset-inclusion, dependence, and LLN assumptions.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates design-based unbiasedness, consistency, asymptotic normality, and conservative variance estimation, the right narrative discipline for this inference boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal estimand is a linear functional of fixed potential outcomes -> randomization supplies an unbiased linear estimator -> inference requires a design-based CLT -> an observable higher-order upper bound must consistently studentize that estimator

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce structured randomization statistics to finite-population sampling or permutation arrays and verify maximal-coordinate and nondegenerate-variance conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The numerator is still a fixed linear randomization statistic even though the proposed denominator uses higher-order observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Control the mean-square error of an inverse-probability variance-bound estimator through assignment dependence, outcome boundedness, and coefficient norms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required LLN is a higher-order analogue of this quadratic consistency proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine local-dependence normal approximation with randomization-based inverse-probability variance estimation under an exposure mapping.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Assignment-specific observed-coordinate sets induce the same kind of local joint-observability constraints as network exposures.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when a strict higher-degree improvement in a finite binary randomized experiment tensorizes under independent replication, including the scaling of objectives, certificates, degree, and assignment-level implementations.

source_refs.claim: Treats arbitrary design--linear-estimator--variance-bound triplets through matrix analysis but gives no product-design law for nonquadratic bound gaps.
source_refs.author: Joel A. Middleton

source_refs.claim: Optimizes design-compatible quadratic bounds and studies large-sample estimability, without characterizing products of higher-order observable spaces.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Develops finite-population CLTs for several structured randomization schemes but does not propagate exact variance-bound optimization gaps across independent blocks.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Matrix treatments do not determine how the full observable-subset space behaves under a product assignment law. Replication introduces estimator normalization and cross-block terms, while primal domination cones and dual measures may add, factor, or need constant padding depending on which lower-degree components are retained. The scan found asymptotic results for structured designs but no exact theorem transporting a nonquadratic-versus-low-degree gap together with its rational dual certificate and unbiased implementation through independent products.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A product-design theorem identifying the tensorized observable Mobius space and giving exact formulas for the replicated unrestricted and degree-restricted optima, dual witnesses, separation, and block-scaled unbiased bound estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its design--estimator--bound triplet language explains why an exact small-design phenomenon should be transported to a growing sequence of experiments.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A variance bound depends jointly on design and estimator -> arbitrary triplets need a common algebra -> one finite block can exhibit a strict higher-degree gain -> independent replication asks whether that gain survives at inferential scale

method_exemplars.technique: Separate the known variance coefficient from compatible slack and certify optimality with a monotone supporting objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Tensorization can be attacked by constructing additive primal slacks and correspondingly scaled supporting dual weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce structured randomization statistics to finite-population arrays and verify a Lindeberg-type maximal-term condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Independent replication is the bridge from an exact finite gap to a correctly normalized asymptotic statement.

open_problems.open_problem: For two-arm, two-block adaptive complete randomization, determine exactly when nodewise observable-margin variance extrema admit one globally consistent fixed-potential-outcome completion and quantify the cross-history compatibility gap otherwise.

source_refs.excerpt: solve the two-arm, two-block finite-history case, separating a genuine cross-history obstruction
The rectangular relaxation permits an independent convexified coupling at each possible history node.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Nodewise transport programs may choose mutually incompatible couplings because the same labeled units and fixed potential outcomes must serve every history generated by one predictable assignment rule. Sharpness at each node therefore need not imply ex-ante sharpness on the history tree. The first proof step that must change is to replace independent nodewise couplings by a single root-to-leaf completion polytope with shared unit variables and nonanticipativity constraints.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite history-tree LP whose projection equals the ex-ante feasible predictable-variance set, with a necessary-and-sufficient zero-gap criterion and an exact rational two-block primal-dual witness whenever the rectangular envelope is strictly too wide.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from history-dependent assignment to finite-population covariance provides the natural destination framing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive allocation makes assignment laws history-dependent -> estimator errors form martingale differences -> nodewise residual margins bound conditional variance -> global sharpness requires one completion consistent across all histories

method_exemplars.technique: Represent missing cross-world dependence by a multi-marginal transport program and prove that coupling extrema exhaust the identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each history node has this residual-coupling structure; the new proof must glue the programs using shared ex-ante variables.

method_exemplars.technique: Use rearrangement bounds to obtain sharp variance endpoints and consistent endpoint estimators under complete randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the static two-arm base case that the history-tree characterization must recover.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a finite ambiguity class of exposure mappings, characterize the variance bounds that are design-estimable and conservative for every candidate mapping and determine their robust Pareto-admissible frontier.

source_refs.excerpt: misspecified exposures is its own stated open problem

open_problems.why_unsolved: The quadratic HMS framework assumes that the exposure mapping is correctly specified, whereas a misspecified mapping can still define a statistically estimable contrast without validating its intended causal interpretation. Robust validity cannot be checked in one fixed observable cone because observable coordinates and latent products vary with the mapping. The missing proof step is to characterize intersections or common refinements of mapping-specific Boolean spaces and decide whether domination is mappingwise or must hold on a larger joint schedule class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An intersection-cone or common-refinement theorem for mapping-specific observable Mobius spaces, followed by a finite robust-domination LP and dual characterization of every bound conservative over the declared exposure-mapping ambiguity class.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates exposure-defined estimands from assumptions validating the exposure model, the conceptual distinction the robust-bound problem must preserve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Analysts summarize interference through exposure labels -> labels may remain statistically usable when causally misspecified -> guarantees tied to one mapping can fail -> seek variance bounds valid over a declared mapping ambiguity class

method_exemplars.technique: Separate exposure definitions from causal assumptions and compare the estimands induced under correct and misspecified mappings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the mapping-ambiguity semantics required before a common conservative-bound class can be defined.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode estimability and conservativeness as convex constraints on observable bound coefficients and certify admissibility by domination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The robust problem preserves this optimization structure but imposes simultaneous constraints from several exposure mappings.

open_problems.open_problem: For the heterogeneous-Bernoulli bipartite exposure estimator, determine whether its graph-only variance envelope is the exact supremum over centered bounded binary schedules and, if not, characterize the Pareto-improvable slack.

source_refs.excerpt: add a sharpness theorem showing V_env is the exact supremum ... over bounded centered outcome schedules
Investigate whether V_env is sharp or constant-factor sharp as a worst-case bounded-outcome variance envelope

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted proposal optimizes a graph-only upper envelope but does not prove that its separate absolute-value relaxations can be attained jointly by one centered schedule. Shared intervention neighborhoods couple signs of within-arm and cross-arm products, so coordinatewise maximization may be infeasible. The missing step is an exact binary-schedule program retaining centering and joint sign constraints, followed by comparison with the existing envelope.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite Boolean primal-dual program for worst-case design variance over centered binary schedules, plus either an equality criterion or a rational strict-gap certificate and the induced Pareto improvement of the graph-only envelope.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames design-based bipartite inference through exposure probabilities, variance, and conservative standard errors before turning to richer designs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bipartite interventions induce product exposure events -> overlap determines estimator variance -> heterogeneous probabilities may improve design -> exact optimization requires the true bounded-schedule variance envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Retain joint potential-outcome coupling constraints when maximizing randomization variance instead of maximizing covariance terms separately.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same joint-attainability issue determines whether the heterogeneous bipartite envelope is sharp.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize conservative estimable bounds under design-induced missing products and construct their inverse-probability implementations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The graph-only envelope is one conservative rule whose admissibility must be tested against the complete observable class.

literature_map:
Neyman's finite-population randomization framework is the foundational source of the unidentified treatment-effect covariance in difference-in-means variance.
Aronow--Samii (2013, Survey Methodology) isolates zero pairwise inclusion probabilities and supplies a universally conservative correction for nonmeasurable designs.
Aronow--Middleton (2013, Journal of Causal Inference) develops broad design-unbiased linear effect estimators and conservative variance formulas under known assignment.
Aronow--Green--Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1405.6555) obtains asymptotically sharp complete-randomization bounds through extremal coupling of observed marginals.
Aronow--Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics; arXiv:1305.6156) separates design, exposure mapping, and estimand under interference and proves local-dependence inference.
Lu (2019, Statistical Methods in Medical Research; arXiv:1711.04432) shows that binary inclusion-exclusion identities can sharpen randomization variance bounds in a 2-by-2 factorial design.
Middleton (2018, arXiv:1803.06011) develops regression adjustment and tighter variance bounds for arbitrary designs in a general matrix language.
Middleton (2021, arXiv:2109.09220) unifies linear estimators, arbitrary designs, and quadratic variance-bound estimation through matrix analysis.
Harshaw--Middleton--Savje (2026, JASA; arXiv:2112.01709) is closest: it gives a quadratic characterization, admissible quadratic bounds, OPT-VB, Horvitz--Thompson implementation, and a school-data empirical illustration rather than a reanalysis of original causal conclusions.
The scan found no all-degree Boolean Mobius characterization, no cubic-versus-quartic exact separation, and no exact rational observable-margin dual in the arbitrary-design literature.
Chattopadhyay--Imbens (2024, arXiv:2409.12498) emphasizes that Neyman's variance estimator has no unique natural extension to complex designs and develops imputation and contrast routes.
Mikhaeil--Green (2024, arXiv:2411.00191) extends sharp marginal-coupling bounds to regression adjustment under complete-randomization asymptotics.
Li--Ding (2017, JASA; arXiv:1610.04821) supplies finite-population CLT machinery but not consistency of higher-order bound estimators.
Harshaw--Savje--Wang (2022, arXiv:2210.08698) gives a broad design-based linear-functional framework with unbiasedness, asymptotic normality, and conservative variance estimation.
Yu--Zhu--Liu (2025, Statistics in Medicine; arXiv:2401.16667) develops sharp variance estimation and causal-bootstrap refinements for stratified designs, reinforcing that denominator validity is separate from a finite bound certificate.

The closest live entry was active exp_mixed_design_degree_frontier; its resolved positive-hard-family OEQ was not recycled, while its remaining all-procedure and signed-boundary questions were checked for overlap.
Downgraded exp_ego_cluster_exposure_clt supplied the direct HMS-adjacent boundary: completion sharpness does not establish optimality over observable quadratic or higher-order bounds.
Failed exp_njack_inflation_frontier explicitly records misspecified-exposure variance optimization as open; its refuted square-root inflation conjecture was excluded.
Failed exp_block_adaptive_ot_variance_envelope reviews angle0_v1--v6 repeatedly identify cross-history completion compatibility, especially the two-arm two-block case, as unresolved.
Accepted exp_bipartite_minimax_design reviews angle0_v2--v3 leave exact bounded-schedule sharpness of the graph-only variance envelope open.
Accepted exp_snipe_degree_frontier leaves heterogeneous-propensity cancellation geometry, matched rates, variance estimation, and studentization outside scope.
Accepted exp_design_pm1_exactness_boundary leaves an exact implementability transition open, while downgraded exp_prognostic_design_admissibility documents exponential exact-program enumeration.
The rejected-angle archives for exp_dte_minimax_comp_frontier, exp_sparsepool_graph_discovery_frontier, and exp_two_wave_endpoint_poisson_minimax were inspected and yielded no closer variance-bound opportunity.
